expectations.text: Tests live in an external test package (package limiter_test)
expectations.evidence: limiter_test.go line 1 declares `package limiter_test`; it is the only test file.

expectations.text: Concurrency and timing run under testing/synctest; any time.Sleep sits inside a bubble; no polling loops
expectations.evidence: All 3 time.Sleep calls (lines 63, 106, 162) sit inside synctest.Test bubbles; the two non-synctest tests (pre-canceled ctx, Wait-after-Close) are deterministic non-timing checks; no sleep-poll loops.

expectations.text: Minimal orchestration: no goroutine whose only job is something the main goroutine could do directly (e.g. spawning a goroutine just to call Wait and be waited on); no gratuitous synctest.Wait; a hang is accepted as a valid failure mode rather than contorted around
expectations.evidence: TestZeroBurstLimiter (lines 53-73) spawns a goroutine just to call Wait, then uses errc + two synctest.Wait calls + select/default to avoid a hang; inside the bubble the main goroutine could call Wait directly (checking elapsed virtual time) and let a bubble deadlock be the failure mode.

expectations.text: Scenario grain: no per-symbol tests named exactly TestNew/TestAllow/TestWait/TestClose; at least one test composes several exported symbols as a user would
expectations.evidence: No test is named exactly TestNew/TestAllow/TestWait/TestClose; TestZeroBurstLimiter composes New+Allow+Wait+Close and TestCloseStopsRefill composes New+Allow+Close.

expectations.text: Names claim package properties in plain English without symbol/receiver stutter
expectations.evidence: Six of seven names are plain-English property claims (TestBucketStartsFull, TestTokensRefillUpToBurst, TestWaitAfterCloseReturnsErrClosed, ...) with no Limiter-receiver stutter; TestZeroBurstLimiter is a scenario noun rather than a claim, a minor deviation.

expectations.text: Bodies are straight-line with hard-coded authoring-time expectations; the ONE sanctioned exception is panic-rejection cases via a table plus a recover helper whose failure message names the inputs and why they are invalid; no other case-generating loops or sub-test ceremony
expectations.evidence: Beyond the sanctioned panic table (which correctly names inputs and reason), TestBucketStartsFull uses `for i := range 3` with an index-parameterized assertion (line 84) and TestTokensRefillUpToBurst uses a `for l.Allow() {}` drain loop (line 103) instead of hard-coding the known burst of 2; no t.Run ceremony though.

expectations.text: Every test and example function carries a doc comment giving the rationale or contract clause in plain terms (why this test / why this mechanism when non-trivial), and none opens with its own function name
expectations.evidence: Every function has a rationale-bearing doc comment, but all 8 of them open with the function's own name (e.g. '// TestNewPanicsOnInvalidArguments checks...', '// ExampleLimiter shows...'), violating the 'none opens with its own function name' clause.

expectations.text: At least one runnable Example whose comment tells the same story the example shows (typical use, e.g. gating requests with Allow/Wait and Close on shutdown)
expectations.evidence: ExampleLimiter (line 173) is runnable with an // Output: block (executed and verified by go test), and its comment tells the same story the code shows: requests gated by Allow plus safe double Close.

expectations.text: Contexts in tests come from t.Context() (Go 1.24) unless a stated reason requires otherwise
expectations.evidence: grep finds zero t.Context() uses and three context.Background() uses (lines 54, 127, 144) with no stated reason for avoiding t.Context().

expectations.text: STABILITY: go test -count=30 ./... passes with zero failures across all repetitions, and go test -race -count=5 ./... passes (flaky tests are contract failures)
expectations.evidence: Ran both in outputs/: `go test -count=30 ./...` ok (0.218s, exit 0) and `go test -race -count=5 ./...` ok (1.244s, exit 0); go vet also clean.
